limitations: Default global norm1 is a prospective, unfrozen optimization choice. Objective coefficients, batch/accumulation schedule, optimizer parameters, clipping frequency and reporting must be specified and reviewed before training.

Global clipping protects this observed float32 squaring overflow but does not guarantee stable future weights, moments, updates or learning. Existing optimizer moments are not inspected or repaired by the helper.

A clipped or zero admitted gradient does not certify an eligible target, useful supervision or absence of an optimizer update. The scheduler must manage eligibility separately; momentum or other optimizer state is outside admission.
Very small positive bounds can underflow all candidates to zero, as explicitly observed at5e-324. Clipping can also change the relative practical contribution of losses through float32 quantization.

The helper is not transactional across optimizer.step or arbitrary failures while assigning gradients. It cannot recover a native/hardware failure during assignment; preparation atomicity and exclusive ownership are the reviewed scope.
Dense float32 gradients only. AMP, distributed gradient buckets, sparse optimizer paths, graph-captured/differentiable optimizers and GPU behavior are not validated here.

Synthetic CPU tests only: no native emulator, Atari or calibration archives, GPU, live learner update, benchmark or gate. Synthetic optimizer steps are limited test mechanics and do not authorize training.
